gaps.sentence: Barely ___ the survey published when the complaints arrived.
gaps.explanation: Barely had X happened when Y — like hardly… when.

gaps.sentence: Not only ___ the tickets expensive, but they were also sold out.
gaps.explanation: Not only were the tickets… — inversion with 'be' needs no auxiliary.

gaps.sentence: Never have I ___ such a stubborn refusal.
gaps.explanation: Inversion: Never have I + past participle — never adds emphasis.

gaps.sentence: Only by training every day ___ she hope to qualify.
gaps.explanation: 'Only by training every day could she hope …' — inverted modal.

gaps.sentence: To ___ did you address that complaint, exactly?
Only since the redesign ___ the app gained new users.
gaps.explanation: 'Only since the redesign has the app gained …' — perfect inversion.

gaps.sentence: Not until every passenger had been evacuated ___ the captain leave the ship.
gaps.explanation: 'Not until … did the captain leave …' — inverted past simple.

gaps.sentence: ___ as it may sound, the machine still works perfectly.
gaps.explanation: Adjective + as + subject + verb = although it sounds strange.
